claims.text: Magnetron sputtering can produce a homogeneous amorphous or near-amorphous AlTiVNb high-entropy-alloy film.
A homogeneous amorphous or near-amorphous lightweight HEA can simultaneously exhibit high mechanical strength and corrosion resistance.
A homogeneous amorphous or near-amorphous lightweight HEA will also exhibit improved high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Allowing phase segregation or partial crystallization in the same alloy will eliminate the synergistic mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation benefits.
Changing cooling or solidification rate can generate either a uniform amorphous structure or a segregated polycrystalline structure at identical composition.
The beneficial structural mediator is a highly uniform amorphous or near-amorphous microstructure with pronounced lattice distortion.
High mixing entropy combined with rapid solidification suppresses long-range order and phase segregation.
Disorder, nanostructure, and lattice distortion contribute to the high strength of amorphous AlTiVNb HEA films.
Lattice distortion enhances strength by impeding dislocation motion.
Chemical disorder, the cocktail effect, and a homogeneous amorphous structure contribute to the corrosion resistance of AlTiVNb HEA films.
A homogeneous amorphous structure promotes formation of a continuous, stable passive oxide film.
The proposed passive oxide film enhances both aqueous corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Phase boundaries and segregated regions act as weak spots that compromise mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation properties.
Relative to conventionally processed material of the same composition, rapidly solidified amorphous material will have greater compressive strength or hardness.
Relative to conventionally processed material of the same composition, rapidly solidified amorphous material will have lower corrosion current density in 3.5% NaCl.
Relative to conventionally processed material of the same composition, rapidly solidified amorphous material will show lower oxidation weight gain or oxidation rate at high temperature.
An amorphous AlTiVNb HEA film exhibited compressive strength up to 3.6 GPa and deformability approaching 58%.
An amorphous AlTiVNb HEA film exhibited a corrosion current density of 4.90 × 10^-8 A/cm2 and a potential of -0.234 V in 3.5% NaCl, comparable to 316L stainless steel.
Below a critical cooling-rate threshold, compositional inhomogeneity will compromise lattice-distortion strengthening and uniform oxide-film formation.

contradictions.description: The material is described as amorphous, which lacks a conventional long-range crystal lattice, while pronounced 'lattice distortion' and dislocation impediment are presented as central mechanisms without clarifying how those crystalline concepts apply to the amorphous state.
